definition: How high or low a sound seems to the listener; a higher frequency gives a higher pitch.
How loud a sound seems to the listener; for a sound of a given frequency, a larger amplitude gives a louder sound.
A sound reflected from a surface, heard after the original sound; when you hear your own echo, it has travelled to the surface and back, twice the distance to the surface.
Sound whose frequency is above $20\ \text{kHz}$, too high for humans to hear; in the same medium it travels at the same speed as audible sound.
A region of a longitudinal wave, such as sound, where the particles are closer together than normal, so the pressure is higher than normal.
A region of a longitudinal wave, such as sound, where the particles are further apart than normal, so the pressure is lower than normal.

Finding the depth of water or the distance to an object by sending out pulses of ultrasound and timing their echoes; distance = speed × echo time ÷ 2, where the echo time runs from sending a pulse to receiving its echo.
